evals.name: tiny-script-no-trigger
evals.prompt: Write me a Python script that renames every .jpeg file in a folder to .jpg.
evals.expected_output: Neither skill runs a workflow. No track question, no interview, no brief, no docs folder. The script is written directly.
assertions: does not ask which track
does not create project-brief.md, AGENTS.md, or any docs/ file
produces the requested script

evals.name: app-with-accounts-two-step-flow
evals.prompt: I have an idea for an app. Students at my university log in and book time on shared lab equipment, and two lab staff approve or reject the requests. I'm using a coding agent to build it. Can you help me plan it?
evals.expected_output: ovc-discover asks one track question first, interviews in small batches, raises security and asks (does not assume) about laws/policies, shows the full brief before saving, saves a brief with ovc-brief-version: 2 and a track, and offers three handoff options. ovc-specify then validates the header, generates documents for the track with requirement IDs, a traceability table, a STRIDE table with Verified by evidence and all four statuses, a short AGENTS.md with a Definition of done, docs/DECISIONS.md, a pointer file only for the named tool, and passes scripts/check_specs.py.
assertions: first substantive question is the single level-and-size question
brief header contains ovc-brief-version: 2, a valid track, and a valid level
brief includes Success looks like and Assumptions & risks sections
the full draft is shown and confirmed before the file is saved
handoff lists new session, clear context, and continue here
PRD requirement IDs all appear in the BUILD_PLAN traceability table
STRIDE table has a Verified by column and no Mitigated row without typed evidence
no pointer file is created for a tool the person did not name
check_specs.py exits 0
brief includes Performance & efficiency goals and Builder & learning goals sections
BUILD_PLAN ends with a Handover phase and AGENTS.md Definition of done requires docs/GUIDE.md
variants: brief with ovc-brief-version: 3 is rejected with a clear message
brief with no header is treated as v1 and an upgrade is offered, not silently accepted

evals.name: existing-repo-brownfield
evals.prompt: This is my existing Flask project. Can you document it for an AI coding agent and tell me if there are security problems?
evals.expected_output: ovc-specify brownfield mode: read-only scan, permission asked before executing repo code, secrets never printed, outputs AGENTS.md, docs/SECURITY.md, docs/GAPS.md, docs/DECISIONS.md; no PRD/ARCHITECTURE/BUILD_PLAN; existing instruction files not overwritten without agreement; passes check_specs.py --mode brownfield.
assertions: ovc-discover does not trigger
no source files are modified
no secret values appear in the output
GAPS.md has ranked gap rows with typed evidence, or states No gaps found with what was checked
PRD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and BUILD_PLAN.md are not created
check_specs.py --mode brownfield exits 0

evals.name: beginner-stack-advice
evals.prompt: I want to build a website where people can post and search for second-hand textbooks. I'm new to coding and I don't know what language to use. I want it to be fast and I want the AI to make as few mistakes as possible.
evals.expected_output: ovc-discover at beginner level explains that speed, AI-reliability, and readability are separate questions, recommends one mainstream typed stack plus one alternative with reasons, defines unfamiliar terms with concept cards, converts 'fast' into default numeric targets, asks the learning-goal question, and records the technology decision with the alternative and when to revisit.
assertions: gives exactly one recommendation and one alternative, at most three options
does not recommend a steep language such as Rust or C++ as a beginner default for speed
states that language is rarely the speed limit for a database-backed website
turns fast into numbers and labels them defaults
records the technology choice in Key decisions with alternative and revisit condition
does not quote benchmark numbers without their limits
variants: expert who names their own stack gets no stack advice, only real gaps flagged once

evals.name: explain-what-was-built
evals.prompt: We've finished building it. I don't really understand what the AI wrote. Can you explain what we built and what each part does?
evals.expected_output: ovc-explain writes docs/GUIDE.md from the real code: tour, walkthrough, requirements coverage with honest statuses and evidence, measured-or-Not-measured performance, security status that lists open items, check-yourself questions with code pointers, and a what-I-could-not-verify section; the guide passes check_guide.py.
assertions: discover and specify do not trigger
no source file is modified and no secret value is printed
every path and file:line in the guide exists
every requirement ID is covered with Done, Partial, or Not built
Done entries carry typed evidence and cited tests exist
performance cells are measured with evidence or exactly Not measured
security status lists open or unverified items
check_guide.py exits 0
